current.text: He opted into a 1-year, 49 million USD contract after he could not find a new team. It is the final year of his deal, and the Kings have no interest in extending him.
He is a projected starter for the Kings, next to Acuff, Hunter, Murray and Sabonis. Nobody is pushing that group for a starting spot.
Schroder, Westbrook and DeRozan are gone. He now shares the ball mainly with Sabonis.
Coach Ham calls him the Kings' second best player behind Sabonis. Ham says LaVine's scoring gravity helps the young players.
Experts expect more usage and more ball handling than last season. One expects him to start and play 30+ minutes.
Last season he converted only 46.7% of his potential assists while playing with poor shooters. With Westbrook and DeRozan gone, his assists could rise a lot.
His role is unclear. He could be traded, bought out or benched, because the Kings are focused on the future and could pull his minutes. Many experts call this the main risk to his value.
The Kings are in a teardown and rebuild and are projected near the bottom of the West. They still need to stay out of the relegation zone and may try to win games, which supports his minutes.

He is still a good offensive player and goes late in many drafts. Experts call him good value at his round 9 to 10 price. He could easily be a top-80 player, and he is a top-50 player when he is firing.
Two experts rank him in tier 8. They say he should easily beat that ranking per game and would be two tiers higher without the Kings risk.
In 9-cat mock drafts he went at pick 107 in a 10-team league and at pick 114 in a 12-team league.

durable.text: His category strengths are 3PM, FT%, points and FG% for a guard. He is weak in steals, blocks and rebounds, but none of these is a league outlier.
He shot well even when he was used mainly as a spot-up shooter.
He is a poor defender and is 31 years old.

note: LaVine is cheap: Yahoo values him at 4 USD (rank 99), ESPN at 0 USD (rank 158), and he cost 12 USD in our league last season. That makes him a good late target at 1 to 5 USD for any build, since 3PM, FT% and points from a guard with a good FG% hurt no punt. He played only 25 and 39 games in two of the last three seasons, and his role in Sacramento is uncertain. Check early whether he starts with 30+ minutes and gets the bigger ball-handling role (ESPN projects 20.5 points on 14.9 shots, Yahoo only 17.0 on 12.1), and watch for trade or buyout news before the 2027-03-04 deadline.
